identity.description: Telegram Messenger's developer platform: the Bot API (HTTP, bot tokens issued via BotFather) and the MTProto-based Telegram API (api_id/api_hash, with TDLib as the official client library). Docs live at core.telegram.org.
identity.identity_notes: core.telegram.org is Telegram's official developer documentation for the Bot API and the Telegram API (MTProto), which matches the product named in the task. telegram.org itself was not fetched, so official_website is null.

auth.token_refresh: Bot tokens can be regenerated through BotFather, per the Bot API page. No OAuth refresh flow was found.
auth.scopes_notes: Bot API: a bot token is placed in the request URL path (https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME). There are no OAuth scopes. The MTProto client API uses api_id and api_hash to identify the app, then the user logs in with a phone-number account; that login flow was not verified in detail.

access.production_restrictions: Third-party client apps must comply with the API Terms of Service. The api_id page describes no approval or review step. Each phone number can hold only one api_id. The sample api_id in open-source code is for testing only and must not be used for publishing.

resources: Chats and chat administration (per third-party listings)
api.rate_limits: Per the Bot FAQ: about 30 messages per second broadcast; one message per second per single chat; 20 messages per minute in a group.
api.limitations: Bot API bots only see private chats with users, and in groups they see only commands unless privacy mode is disabled or they are admins. Bots cannot read arbitrary user DMs. Rate limits apply (about 1 message per second per chat, 20 per minute per group). Breadth is Medium because the verified Bot API surface covers messaging, updates and settings; the full method count (reported by third parties as 150+) was not verified from Telegram's own pages. The MTProto client API is a separate, lower-level protocol.

open_questions: No official Telegram MCP server was found. Searches and the TelegramMessenger GitHub org page (10 of 27 repos shown) listed none. The official status is based on absence of evidence.
Full Bot API method count and per-method details were not verified from Telegram's own pages. The Bot API page was truncated after about 100k characters.
Whether bot tokens are issued only through BotFather with no sandbox or test environment was not confirmed. Telegram's test DC availability was not checked.
Official SDK list was not confirmed. TDLib is named by Telegram as the official client library, but no official Bot API SDK list was checked.
The MTProto user login flow (phone, code, 2FA) and any JWT/service-account option were not verified.
Several claims rely on summarized WebFetch output rather than verbatim page text. Quotes should be re-checked against the live pages before production use.
Third-party MCP version claims conflict (Bot API v9.6 vs v10.2) and are unverified.

rationale: Self-serve test credentials (free self serve) and a documented CLI/library/REST interface.
